title: Render Prop / Slot Decoupler
problemStatement: Implement `createSlotContainer(renderHeader, renderBody)` that accepts slot render functions and generates UI output without tightly coupling internal layout state to children.
interviewTrap: Creating slot components inside the render loop rather than passing them from outer scope recreates DOM nodes on every render.

testCases.name: Supplies internal state to header and body slots
testCases.testFn: const container = createSlotContainer(s => 'TITLE: ' + s.user, s => 'CONTENT: ' + s.user); return container({ user: 'Admin' });

testCases.name: Decouples slots cleanly
testCases.testFn: const container = createSlotContainer(() => 'header', s => s.count * 10); return container({ count: 10 }).body;

testCases.name: Handles static content slots
testCases.testFn: const container = createSlotContainer(() => 'Static Header', () => 'Static Body'); return container({}).header;

details.name: Supplies internal state to header and body slots

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Passing an expensive component as the `children` prop `<Parent><ExpensiveTree /></Parent>` prevents `ExpensiveTree` from re-rendering when `Parent`'s state changes! Because `ExpensiveTree` is evaluated in the grandparent's render scope, its element reference is identical across `Parent` re-renders.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Inverting Control via Render Props.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Inverting Control via Render Props maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

edgeCasesHandled: Creating slot components inside the render loop rather than passing them from outer scope recreates DOM nodes on every render.
